plain_english: That Anuttara-formed one, by his own desire to manifest all this world, vibrated; that first vibration is called the Śiva-principle by those who know it.
sanskrit_cite: यदयमनुत्तरमूर्तिर्नजेच्छयाखिलमिदं जगत्स्रष्टुम्। पस्पन्दे स स्पन्दः प्रथमः शिवतत्त्वमुच्यते तज्ज्ञैः॥१॥

plain_english: Will itself — transparent, ever-co-inherent, being — is power: the seed of the entire world of moving and unmoving things, hidden in herself.
sanskrit_cite: इच्छा सैव स्वच्छा सन्ततसमवायिनी सती शक्तिः। सचराचरस्य जगतो बीजं निखिलस्य निजनिलीनस्य॥२॥

plain_english: Having fully covered with the Self the world emitted by own will-power, abiding — he indeed, devoted to all grace, is called Sadāśiva.
sanskrit_cite: स्वेच्छाशक्त्युद्गीर्णं जगदात्मतया समाच्छाद्य। निवसन् स एव निखिलानुग्रहनिरतः सदाशिवोऽभिहितः॥३॥

plain_english: Seeing the universe after himself with this-ness, the Lord has become all; that becomes pure knowledge, in which this and I are held non-different.
sanskrit_cite: विश्वं पश्चात्पश्यनिदन्तया निखिलमीश्वरो जातः। सा भवति शुद्धविद्या येदन्ताहन्तयोरभेदमतिः॥४॥

plain_english: Māyā is difference-notion toward all beings born of own portions; always his unbridled power — like the ocean shore — blocks.
sanskrit_cite: माया विभेदबुद्धिर्निजांशजातेषु निखिलजीवेषु। नित्यं तस्य निरङ्कुशविभवं वेलेव वारिधे रुन्धे॥५॥

plain_english: He, by her, of limited form with all powers contracted — this is the Person; like the sun red at dusk, powers withdrawn, unskilled even in self-shining.
sanskrit_cite: स तया परिमितमूर्तिः सङ्कुचितसमस्तशक्तिरेष पुमान्। रविरिव सन्ध्यारक्तः संहृतशक्तिः स्वभासनेऽप्यपटुः॥६॥

plain_english: Complete doership and the rest — many are his powers; through contraction contracted, in the form of kalā and the rest, thus they ascend.
sanskrit_cite: सम्पूर्णकर्तृताद्या बह्व्यः सन्त्यस्य शक्तयस्तस्य। सङ्कोचात्सङ्कुचिताः कलादिरूपेण रूढयन्त्येवम्॥७॥

plain_english: That all-doership, contracted, directed merely at a few things — making him a doer-of-little — is called kalā by name.
sanskrit_cite: तत्सर्वकर्तृता सा सङ्कुचिता कतिपयार्थमात्रपरा। किञ्चित्कर्तारममुं कलयन्ती कीर्त्यते कला नाम॥८॥

plain_english: His all-knowing power, of limited body, directed merely at little to be known — producing knowledge — is declared vidyā by the ancient wise.
sanskrit_cite: सर्वज्ञतास्य शक्तिः परिमिततनुरल्पवेद्यमात्रपरा। ज्ञानमुत्पादयन्ती विद्येति निगद्यते बुधैराद्यैः॥९॥

plain_english: Ever-full satisfaction, his very power, yet limited, being — ever coloring him toward enjoyments — has become raga-principle-ness.
sanskrit_cite: नित्यपरिपूर्णतृप्तिः शक्तिस्तस्यैव परिमिता तु सती। भोगेषु रञ्जयन्ती सततममुं रागतत्त्वतां याता॥१०॥

plain_english: That eternity, his power — having drawn off by giving rise-and-fall — making fixed divisions, is arranged in the form of the time-principle.
sanskrit_cite: सा नित्यतास्य शक्तिर्निकृष्य निधनोदयप्रदानेन। नियतपरिच्छेदकरी कॢप्ता स्यात्कालतत्त्वरूपेण॥११॥

plain_english: Which power of his called autonomy, rich in contraction — that very one, constraining him helplessly fixed in do-and-do-not, became restriction.
sanskrit_cite: यास्य स्वतन्त्रताख्या शक्तिः सङ्कोचशालिनी सैव। कृत्याकृत्येष्ववशं नियतममुं नियमयन्त्यभून्नियतिः॥१२॥

plain_english: The triad-collection of will and the rest — power, quiescent, of contracted form in him; but consisting, being, in the sameness of sattva and the rest whose nature is collected will and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: इच्छादित्रिसमष्टिः शक्तिः शान्तास्य सङ्कुचद्रूपा। सङ्कलितेच्छाद्यात्मकसत्त्वादिकसाम्यरूपिणी तु सती॥१३॥

plain_english: Deemed prakṛti: of the nature of citta whose nature is the fusion of buddhi and the rest; his will, as rajas-formed I-making effecting I-notion, was.
sanskrit_cite: बुद्ध्यादिसामरस्यस्वरूपचित्तात्मिका मता प्रकृतिः। इच्छास्य रजोरूपाहङ्कृतिरासीदहम्प्रतीतिकरी॥१४॥

plain_english: Even knowledge, of sattva-nature, is the cause of determinative cognition — buddhi; its action, dark-formed-bodied, is called mind, the doubting-maker.
sanskrit_cite: ज्ञानापि सत्त्वरूपा निर्णयबोधस्य कारणं बुद्धिः। तस्य क्रिया तमोमयमूर्तिर्मन उच्यते विकल्पकरी॥१५॥

plain_english: With fivefold division beginning with Vāmā, that very god of contracted body — through knowledge-action-tinge predominance became of manifold-object form.
sanskrit_cite: वामादिपञ्चभेदः स एव सङ्कुचितविग्रहो देवः। ज्ञानक्रियोपरागप्राधान्याद्विविधविषयरूपोऽभूत्॥१६॥

plain_english: Ear, eye, touch, tongue, nose are the knowledge-instruments; sound, touch, form, taste, smell — thus the subtle elements.
sanskrit_cite: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनजिह्वाघ्राणानि बोधकरणानि। शब्दस्पर्शौ रूपं रसगन्धौ चेति भूतसूक्ष्माणि॥१७॥

plain_english: This very one, most base-born, even as elemental self, is the Lord of beings; ether, air, fire, water, earth — the five gross elements.
sanskrit_cite: अयमेवातिनिकृष्टो जातो भूतात्मनापि भूतेशः। गगनमनिलश्च तेजः सलिलं भूमिश्च पञ्चभूतानि॥१८॥

plain_english: Beginning with sound, to be known by ear and other instruments — they are the knowns of these; speech was the uttering-maker, the hand would be the instrument-being in taking.
sanskrit_cite: श्रोत्रादिकरणवेद्याः शब्दाद्यास्तानि वेदकान्येषाम्। वचनकरी वागासीत् पाणिः स्यात्करणभूत आदाने॥१९॥

plain_english: In the triad of going, excreting, bliss — foot and the rest as instrument; earth would be smell-possessing, waters naturally fluid, fire.
sanskrit_cite: गमनविसर्गानन्दत्रितये पादादिकं करणम्। गन्धवती भूमिः स्यादापः सांसिद्धिकद्रवास्तेजः॥२०॥

plain_english: Hot touch and formless touch is wind; ether with sound. I praise the Kaula consisting of thirty-six principles, beyond the kula — Śambhu.
sanskrit_cite: उष्णस्पर्शमरूपस्पर्शो वायुरम्बरं सशब्दम्। षट्त्रिंशत्तत्त्वमयं वन्दे कौलं कुलातिगं शम्भुम्॥२१॥
